- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70.0), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% in the immediate follow-up period.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in the 10–15 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for high-sentiment or high-activity periods.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.3), model tends to overestimate upward momentum; cap forecast growth at +1.5% per day unless sentiment > 0.5.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing true price reversals; add 1–2 days of “mean reversion” buffer in forecast if sentiment shifts from negative to positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates final price by 1–3% in 70%+ of cases; apply +1.5% bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
